input.quote: Commerce One warrants that the Software and MarketSite.net Service will perform in substantial accordance with the Documentation, and the media on which the Software is distributed will be free from defects in materials and workmanship under normal use, for a period of sixty (60) days from the Effective Date, but in no event not later than December 31, 1999 (the "Warranty Period").
input.rationale: Section 7.3 gives us an express conformance-to-Documentation warranty plus a no-malicious-code warranty, and Section 7.3's second paragraph provides a real remedy ladder (correct, replace free of charge, and termination with refund of all prepaid fees). The defect is duration: sixty (60) days measured from the Effective Date, with an absolute sunset of December 31, 1999. That is below the fallback of ninety (90) days for software, and because Acceptance Testing under Section 3.1 may run until December 31, 1999, the warranty can expire on or before the date we accept the Software — leaving effectively no post-acceptance coverage. We therefore propose the preferred position: twelve (12) months running from acceptance, with ninety (90) days from acceptance offered as a fallback. Mitigants noted but not sufficient to reach the fallback: Section 11.2 deems continued conformance with specifications after the Warranty Period a material condition, and Section 5.3/Exhibit C provide ongoing support and maintenance. The disclaimer at p0084 is truncated in the document but on its face reaches only implied warranties (merchantability, noninfringement, fitness), so it does not appear to swallow the express warranty; no separate flag raised.

proposal.summary: Extend the Product Warranty Period to twelve (12) months running from acceptance instead of sixty (60) days from the Effective Date with a December 31, 1999 sunset.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need the software warranty to run for twelve (12) months from acceptance; as drafted the sixty (60) day period runs from the Effective Date and expires no later than December 31, 1999, which is the same date by which Acceptance Testing may still be underway, so the warranty could lapse before we accept. We can accept ninety (90) days from acceptance as a fallback.
